scope: Five Go top-level declarations: the historical TestFixtureRoundTrip_Complex, two retained-S/P package structure tests, one CT_Slide decoding test and one Presentation Hidden/save-readback test. The round-trip fixture rows remain subcases. Native tests do not select the canonical visibility case or establish PowerPoint behaviour. Go and Python status is recorded separately.

verifiedAspects: The hidden_slides.pptx row opens the committed Go fixture, adds a new layout-zero slide, sets Hidden true, saves, reopens and requires at least one slide with Hidden true.
The multiple_masters.pptx row adds a slide and requires nonempty Masters and Layouts collections after reopening; it does not assert a second slide master.
gaps: The hidden-slide result does not identify slide 3 of the untouched source or compare all four original slide identities, relationships, qualified versus unqualified visibility attributes and source bytes; the newly added hidden slide can alone satisfy the assertion. Before Go 260eacb, its reader reported S slide 3 hidden from namespaced p:show=0; the current decoder uses only unqualified show. Neither historical nor current reader result establishes PowerPoint behaviour.
Neither row reopens an untouched PowerPoint original in PowerPoint; the multiple-masters input has only one slide master and cannot supply that positive.

verifiedAspects: Both sealed S/P archives have exactly four ordered slide IDs, unique internal relationships and resolved slide parts; S slide 3 alone carries namespaced p:show=0, all slides lack unqualified show, and the input bytes remain unchanged.
gaps: Native ZIP inspection is not a selected canonical Gherkin execution; the absence of PowerPoint confirmation is an evidence classification, not a measured application-visible slide state.

verifiedAspects: In-memory marker, namespace, missing/duplicate/reordered/wrong/external relationships, missing/reused/escaping parts and malformed XML controls fail closed without changing the committed fixtures.
gaps: Corruption controls test the native structural inspector; they do not select the shared case or prove PowerPoint behaviour.

verifiedAspects: Seven decoder variants distinguish missing, namespaced, foreign, unqualified visible/hidden and mixed show attributes; only the unqualified CT_Slide attribute sets Show, including XML readback.
gaps: This type-level test does not select the retained-input Gherkin case, verify both manifest-backed ZIP graphs or measure PowerPoint display state.
